source_text: Illud ergo peccatum, quod ipsum hominem in paradiso in peius mutavit, quia multo est grandius quam iudicare nos possumus, ab omni nascente trahitur [n140] . Quis tibi dixit quoniam peccatum Adae multo fuerit grandius quam Cain? Multo etiam quam Sodomitarum? Multo postremo immanius quam tuum atque Manichaei? Certe in historia nulla istius vanitatis invenitur occasio. Iussum fuerat ut edulio unius arboris abstineret; rudis, imperitus, incautus, sine experimento timoris, sine exemplo iustitiae, suggestu mulieris usurpavit escam, cuius illexerat et suavitas, et venustas. Vide hic transgressionem fuisse mandati. Admissa est praevaricatio una de ceteris, quas diversis temporibus peccantium studia perpetrarunt; non fuit amplius, quam cum populus Israelis interdictis utebatur animalibus. Causa enim peccati haud in qualitate pomi erat, sed in transgressione mandati. Quid ergo tale fecit Adam, ut peccatum eius exstitisse supra aestimationem hominum crimineris? Nisi forte et hoc saecundum mysteria Manichaei, qui a decerptione pomorum et omnium nascentium manus cohibet, ne partem Dei sui laceret, quam corticibus et graminibus opinatur inclusam, tu quoque Adam graviter deliquisse, quia cum esu pomi, Dei tui substantiam laceraverit, arbitraris. O furorem! Quia multo est grandius illud peccatum, quam iudicare nos possumus, ab omni - inquit - nascente trahitur. Maius ergo fuit crimen pomum edere, cum non liceret, quam sanctum Abel parricidali livore confodere, quam hospitum in Sodomis et sexuum iura violare, quam filios suos iam sub lege demoniis immolare, quam innocentes postremo nullius conscios voluntatis, recens opus Dei, diaboli regno subdere, meritisque coniungere, quam Deum iniquitatis arguere, quam honorabiles nuptias tenebrarum principi deputare, postremo parvulos, quia nascantur per generantium non fingo, sed colligo; tu quippe illud peccatum ita universis criminibus maius grandiusque dixisti, ut nullo possit aequiparari reatu. Huius autem tam mali magni, quod omnibus vitiis praeponderat, plenos advenire parvulos asseveras. Bene itaque intelleximus, quod quanto maioris peccati participes sunt, tanto in condemnatione scelestis omnibus praeferantur.
pass_a_gloss: That sin therefore, which changed the human himself in paradise into the worse, because it is much greater than we can judge, is drawn from every one being born. Who told you that Adam's sin was much greater than Cain's? Much even than that of the Sodomites? Finally much more monstrous than yours and Manichaeus's? Certainly in the history no occasion of that vanity is found. It had been commanded that he abstain from the food of one tree; raw, unskilled, incautious, without an experiment of fear, without an example of justice, by the suggestion of a woman he usurped a food whose both sweetness and charm had enticed. See here there was a transgression of a mandate. One prevarication was admitted from the rest, which the studies of those sinning perpetrated at diverse times; it was not more, than when the people of Israel was using forbidden animals. For the cause of the sin was not in the quality of the fruit, but in the transgression of the mandate. What therefore of such a kind did Adam do, that you accuse his sin to have existed above the estimation of humans? Unless perhaps even this according to the mysteries of Manichaeus, who holds back his hands from the plucking of fruits and of all things being born, lest he tear a part of his God, which he opines enclosed in barks and grasses, you also think Adam offended gravely, because with the eating of a fruit he tore the substance of your God. O fury! Because that sin is much greater than we can judge, it is drawn, he says, from every one being born. Greater therefore was the charge to eat a fruit when it was not allowed, than to pierce holy Abel with parricidal envy, than to violate the rights of guests and of the sexes in Sodom, than to immolate one's own sons already under the law to demons, than finally to subject innocents conscious of no will, a recent work of God, to the devil's kingdom, and to join them to deserts, than to accuse God of iniquity, than to assign honorable marriages to the prince of darkness, finally little ones, because they are born through those generating I do not feign, but I gather; for you indeed said that sin so greater and greater than all charges, that it can be equaled by no guilt. But of this so great evil, which outweighs all vices, you assert little ones arrive full. Well therefore we understood, that by how much they are participants of a greater sin, so much in condemnation they are preferred to all the wicked.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae; Blaise Christian marriage as God's work
LS parvulus; Blaise infants as Julian's test case

pass_b_english: ‘That sin which changed the human being for the worse in paradise, because it is far greater than we can judge, is inherited by everyone born’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.34.58). Who told you Adam’s sin was far greater than Cain’s? Far greater than the Sodomites’? Far more monstrous, finally, than yours and Mani’s? Certainly the history supplies no occasion for this empty claim. He had been commanded to abstain from eating the fruit of one tree. Inexperienced, unskilled, unwary, without experience of fear or an example of justice, at the woman’s suggestion he took food whose sweetness and beauty had enticed him (Genesis 3:6). Recognize here a transgression of a command.

A transgression was committed, one among the rest that sinners’ pursuits have perpetrated at different times. It was no greater than when the people of Israel ate forbidden animals (compare Leviticus 11). The cause of sin lay not in the fruit’s quality but in violating the command. What, then, did Adam do to justify your accusation that his sin exceeded human estimation? Unless perhaps, following Mani’s mysteries—he keeps his hands from plucking fruits and growing things, lest he tear a part of his god that he imagines enclosed in bark and plants—you too think Adam sinned gravely because by eating the fruit he tore your god’s substance. What madness!

‘Because that sin is far greater than we can judge,’ he says, ‘it is inherited by everyone born.’ So eating forbidden fruit was a greater crime than stabbing holy Abel out of murderous envy (Genesis 4:8); than violating the rights of guests and the order of the sexes in Sodom (Genesis 19:4–9); than sacrificing one’s children to demons even under the law (Psalm 106:37); than subjecting innocent children, aware of no exercise of will and newly made by God, to the devil’s kingdom and joining them to his deserts; than accusing God of injustice; than assigning honorable marriage to the prince of darkness; finally, than to regard infants as worse than all the ungodly, worse than all pirates, because they are born through their parents’ sexual pleasure?

I do not invent this; I draw the conclusion. You called that sin greater and weightier than all crimes, such that no guilt could equal it. And you assert that infants arrive full of this great evil, which outweighs all vices. We have therefore understood correctly: the greater the sin they share, the more they take precedence in condemnation over all criminals.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
